business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Juniper Green Energy develops, builds, operates and maintains utility scale renewable energy projects through its in-house EPC team and O&M team, and generates revenue through the sale of electricity to various off-takers, including central and state government-backed entities. It commissioned its first solar project of 100 MW (144.97 MWp) in March 2020 and has since expanded to a Total Capacity of 7,910.20 MW (10,247.06 MWp) across 50 projects as at June 30, 2026, comprising operational, under construction contracted and under construction awarded projects. Beyond solar, the portfolio includes wind energy projects and a focus on complex renewable energy projects such as WSH and FDRE projects with BESS.

group_structure.body:
- Juniper Renewable Holdings Pte. - AT Holdings Pte. Ltd. — Corporate Promoter; controlling shareholder of Juniper Renewable: Holds 75.01% of Juniper Renewable

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company manages the end-to-end lifecycle of renewable energy project development in-house across all critical stages: (i) bidding and auction; (ii) site prospecting; (iii) land acquisition and grid permits; (iv) engineering and technology; (v) procurement; (vi) project financing; (vii) plant construction and commissioning; and (viii) O&M. It adopts a selective and strategic approach to auctions backed by regulatory and commercial analysis, and identifies high-potential sites using GIS tools, irradiance datasets and wind resource assessments. A dedicated project development team has built a substantial land bank (more than 12,000 acres for solar and more than 300 WTG locations across Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh) and the business development team has secured surplus grid connectivity beyond that allocated to all Under Construction Projects as at June 30, 2026. Engineering and technology design is handled internally by specialists covering layout, balance of plant, turbine technology and battery storage systems. Procurement is managed through long-term relationships and advance orders with global suppliers. By integrating EPC and O&M functions in-house, the Company retains construction margins typically passed to third-party contractors, which it states enhances control over timelines, cost and quality, enables competitive bids and higher profitability, and allows project designs and technology choices to be tailored to site requirements. Operational Projects have been commissioned ahead of schedule by a weighted average of 147 days, with one solar Operational Project commencing 552 days ahead of schedule and one wind Operational Project 222 days ahead of schedule on a weighted average basis. Strategic long-term supply partnerships as at June 30, 2026 include a WTG supply agreement with Envision, a wind operated electricity generator (WOEG) supply agreement with Suzlon Energy Limited, solar module tie-ups with First Solar (for around 1.60 years), Waaree (for around 2.20 years) and Goldi (for around 2.20 years), inverter supply from Sungrow (India) Private Limited, SVGs tie-up with TBEA Xi'an Electric Technology Co. Ltd. and BESS with Envision. Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management are supported by more than 700 employees working across the projects as at June 30, 2026. The Company is dependent on suppliers for critical components: its top 10 suppliers contributed 84.42%, 79.99% and 87.52% of total purchases for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively; key components are wind turbine generators for wind projects and solar modules and inverters for solar projects; procurement agreements typically require manufacturers to provide warranties against equipment failures and defects for a specified period. Other than as disclosed in the risk factor on price changes in solar modules, wind turbines, inverters and other materials, the Company states it has not faced significant disruptions in the procurement of critical components in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: The Company's renewable energy projects generate revenue as a direct function of the electricity they generate, which is influenced significantly by environmental conditions, irradiation and wind speed. Power generation is highly dependent on weather conditions, and profitability depends not only on observed weather conditions at the project site but also on the consistency of those conditions. Operating results for renewable energy projects vary depending on natural variations from season to season and from year to year, and may also change permanently because of climate change or other factors beyond the Company's control. Electricity output is partially dependent on sunlight/irradiation or wind speed, and generation may decrease under certain environmental conditions including cloudy weather, sandstorms, heavy rainfall, solar eclipses and environmental pollution. The Company engages in regular O&M of its Operational Projects and cleaning of solar modules to minimise the impact of soiling, but cannot assure that such initiatives will offset environmental conditions. The seasonal nature of its energy production can also place additional demands on working capital reserves and borrowing capacity under existing debt, particularly during periods when cash flow from operations is reduced.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build out the contracted and awarded pipeline to convert the 7,910.20 MW (10,247.06 MWp) Total Capacity portfolio of 50 projects into operating assets
- Focus on complex renewable energy projects, such as WSH and FDRE projects with BESS, in addition to standalone solar and wind
- Continue bidding for and winning WSH and FDRE tenders, where the Company is ranked the second largest bidder by capacity won between April 1, 2021 and March 31, 2026
- Deleverage the balance sheet using Issue proceeds by repaying/pre-paying borrowings at the Company and at Subsidiary level
- Complete the commissioning of partially commissioned projects, whose balance capacity remains classified under Under Construction Contracted Projects
- Realise the benefits of listing — enhancement of the Company's visibility and brand name amongst existing and potential customers and creation of a public market for the Equity Shares in India

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: As at June 30, 2026 the Company had 50 projects with Total Capacity of 7,910.20 MW AC (10,247.06 MWp) and 4,563.88 MWh of BESS, of which only 20 projects totalling 1,794.80 MW AC (2,408.91 MWp) with 503.20 MWh BESS were operational. The pipeline therefore consists of 19 Under Construction Contracted Projects of 2,875.40 MW AC (3,656.65 MWp) with 3,010.68 MWh BESS, and 11 Under Construction Awarded Projects of 3,240.00 MW AC (4,181.50 MWp) with 1,050.00 MWh BESS. The under-construction pipeline is weighted to complex formats: WSH accounts for 2,357.90 MW of contracted capacity (1,860.00 MW solar AC, 2,627.25 MWp solar DC and 910.90 MW wind AC) and FDRE for 1,765.63 MW of contracted capacity (1,915.00 MW solar AC, 2,862.50 MWp solar DC, 1,189.50 MW wind AC), versus only 20.00 MW of standalone solar and 220.00 MW of standalone wind. Several projects are partially commissioned, with the balance capacity still under construction — including 50.00 MW of the 150.45 MW Juniper Green Energy Limited project, 90.00 MW of the 120.30 MW Juniper Green Spark Four project, 209.70 MW of the 476.60 MW and 92.40 MW of the 192.40 MW Juniper Green Stellar projects, 70.00 MW of the 90.00 MW Juniper Green Kite project, 26.40 MW of the Juniper Green Power Five project and 25.00 MW of the Juniper Green Spark Ten project. Project configurations for both under-construction buckets are based on internal assessments as at June 30, 2026 and may be modified within permitted timelines under the respective LOAs, PPAs and bidding documents.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Among the top 10 largest renewable IPPs in India by Total Capacity as at March 31, 2026 (Source: CRISIL Report)
- Ranked the second largest bidder in terms of total capacity won in WSH and FDRE tenders concluded between April 1, 2021 and March 31, 2026 (Source: CRISIL Report)
- 96.80% conversion rate for WSH and FDRE tenders won between April 1, 2021 and March 31, 2026 (Source: CRISIL Report)
- In-house EPC team and O&M team used to develop, build, operate and maintain utility scale renewable projects
- Long-term revenue visibility from PPAs typically of 25 years with off-takers including central and state government-backed entities
- Demonstrated scale-up of operational capacity from 660.20 MW AC (920.08 MWp) as at March 31, 2024 to 1,794.80 MW AC (2,408.91 MWp) as at June 30, 2026
- Presence across complex renewable formats — solar, wind, WSH and FDRE with BESS — rather than plain-vanilla solar alone

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Extreme off-taker concentration — The top two off-takers, GUVNL and MSEDCL, collectively contributed 86.06%, 91.11% and 97.00% of revenue from operations for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Loss of any such key commercial relationship could adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
- Single revenue stream — sale of electricity from own projects — A significant portion of revenue from operations is derived from the sale of electricity generated at the Company's projects, leaving no material diversification away from generation.
- Counterparty exposure to state discoms under very long-dated PPAs — As at June 30, 2026 all PPAs are for 25 years save for Juniper Green Ray Two Private Limited's, which is for 20 years, so tariffs and payment performance are locked to state-government-backed off-takers for decades.
- Execution risk on a pipeline far larger than the operating base — Only 1,794.80 MW of 7,910.20 MW Total Capacity was operational as at June 30, 2026; 30 of 50 projects (2,875.40 MW contracted plus 3,240.00 MW awarded) remain under construction, along with 4,060.68 MWh of unbuilt BESS.
- Project configurations are provisional — The proposed configuration for Under Construction Contracted and Awarded Projects is based on internal assessments as at June 30, 2026 and may be modified as per project requirements within permitted timelines under the LOAs, PPAs and bidding documents, so stated MW/MWp/MWh figures may change.
- Leverage and refinancing dependence — Net Proceeds of the Issue are earmarked for repayment/pre-payment of Rs.6,832.35 million of the Company's own borrowings and Rs.7,286.86 million of borrowings at Juniper Green Gamma One, Juniper Green Kite and Juniper Green Power Five, indicating material debt across the group.
- Industry positioning claims rest on a commissioned report — Industry and market data, including the top-10 IPP ranking, second-largest WSH/FDRE bidder ranking and 96.80% conversion rate, are derived from the CRISIL Report exclusively commissioned by and paid for by the Company for the Issue.
- Reliance on non-GAAP measures — The RHP includes non-GAAP financial measures and industry metrics that are not standardised, are not defined under Ind AS/IFRS/US GAAP, and may not be comparable with similarly named measures of other companies.
